uncited: It sets itself apart from static grid methods by dynamically pruning low-visibility voxels and subdividing high-error voxels based on gradient signals, building on the general framework of [Coarse-to-Fine Optimization with Pruning](1153-coarse-to-fine-optimization-with-pruning.md).
**Inputs:** A set of training images with known camera parameters (position, orientation, intrinsics including horizontal FOV $\theta_{\text{fov-x}}$ and image width $W$).
**Outputs:** An optimized sparse voxel grid containing Spherical Harmonic (SH) coefficients for color and density values at grid points.
*   **Grid Point:** Stores raw density values.
Grid points are shared among adjacent voxels (8 corners per voxel).
Source voxels are removed upon subdivision.
Initialization depends on whether the scene is bounded or unbounded.
Initialize a dense grid with $h_{lv}$ levels.
Remove voxels that are not observed by any training image.
Define the **Main Region**: A cuboid centered at the average camera position, with radius equal to the median distance from the center to the cameras.
Define the **Background Region**: Allocate $h_{out}$ levels of background shells enclosing the main region.
Initialize background shells with the coarsest voxel size.
Iteratively subdivide background shell voxels with the highest sampling rate and remove unobserved voxels.
Repeat step 4 until the ratio of the number of background voxels to main region voxels equals $h_{ratio}$.
Every $h_{every}$ iterations, perform Adaptive Pruning and Subdivision.
**Select Voxels:** Select voxels with priority above the top $h_{percent}$ percentile.
*   Subdivide selected voxels into 8 children.
*   **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of voxels and training iterations.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Scales with the number of active voxels.
It is part of the SVRaster framework, designed for real-time rendering of high-fidelity radiance fields.
